# creditor

Exploratory R bindings to [Loro](https://loro.dev), a Rust library of
conflict-free replicated data types (CRDTs). Replicas of a document edit
independently, exchange updates as raw vectors, and converge to the same
contents. Text (including rich text marks and cursors), map, list,
movable list, counter, and tree containers are supported, and they can
be nested. Documents keep their full history, which can be listed,
compared, checked out, and reverted. Exports can be full or shallow
snapshots, incremental updates, or JSON. Subscriptions report changes as
they are committed, an undo manager reverses local edits, and an
ephemeral store shares presence state such as cursors.

See
[`vignette("containers", package = "creditor")`](https://rundel.github.io/creditor/articles/containers.md)
for a tour of each container type and how it merges concurrent edits.

## Installation

Building from source needs a Rust toolchain: cargo and `rustc >= 1.85`.

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("rundel/creditor")
```

## Example

Two replicas edit the same text concurrently and then merge.

``` r
library(creditor)

# Replica `a` starts the document with some text
a = loro_doc()
text_insert(a, 1, "Hello")

# Replica `b` starts from a full snapshot of `a`
b = loro_doc()
doc_import(b, doc_export(a))

# Both replicas edit the text independently, without syncing
text_insert(a, 6, " world")
text_insert(b, 1, ">> ")

# Each replica sends the other the updates it is missing
doc_import(b, doc_export_updates(a, from = doc_version(b)))
doc_import(a, doc_export_updates(b, from = doc_version(a)))

# Both edits are kept and the replicas agree
text_get(a)
#> [1] ">> Hello world"
text_get(b)
#> [1] ">> Hello world"
```

Containers nest: a map or list can hold plain values or child
containers, each of which merges independently. New containers are made
with
[`loro_text()`](https://rundel.github.io/creditor/reference/loro_text.md),
[`loro_list()`](https://rundel.github.io/creditor/reference/loro_text.md),
[`loro_map()`](https://rundel.github.io/creditor/reference/loro_text.md),
and friends, and stored like any other value.

``` r
doc = loro_doc()

# A map works like a named list
note = doc_map(doc, "note")

# A plain value is replaced whole when edited concurrently
note$title = "Groceries"

# Child containers merge concurrent edits to their contents
note$items = loro_list("milk", "eggs")
note$body = loro_text("Buy before Friday")

# Edit a child container in place
list_push(note$items, "bread")

str(doc_value(doc))
#> List of 1
#>  $ note:List of 3
#>   ..$ body : chr "Buy before Friday"
#>   ..$ items:List of 3
#>   .. ..$ : chr "milk"
#>   .. ..$ : chr "eggs"
#>   .. ..$ : chr "bread"
#>   ..$ title: chr "Groceries"
```

Text can carry marks, and a cursor keeps pointing at the same character
as the text changes.

``` r
doc = loro_doc()
text = doc_text(doc)
text_insert(text, 1, "Hello world")

# Mark characters 1 to 5 ("Hello") as bold
text_mark(text, 1, 5, bold = TRUE)

# A cursor at the "w" of "world" (character 7)
cursor = text_cursor(text, 7)

# Rewrite the text; only the differences are applied, so the mark and cursor survive
text_update(text, "Hello brave new world")

# The text as runs of characters with their marks
str(text_delta(text))
#> List of 2
#>  $ :List of 2
#>   ..$ insert    : chr "Hello"
#>   ..$ attributes:List of 1
#>   .. ..$ bold: logi TRUE
#>  $ :List of 1
#>   ..$ insert: chr " brave new world"

# The cursor has moved with the "w", which is now character 17
cursor_pos(doc, cursor)
#> [1] 17
```

Every version stays reachable.

``` r
# Two commits, each labeled with a message
doc = loro_doc()
text = doc_text(doc)
text_insert(text, 1, "Hello")
doc_commit(doc, "greeting")
text_insert(text, 6, " world")
doc_commit(doc, "audience")

# One row per change
changes = doc_changes(doc)
changes[, c("lamport", "length", "message")]
#>   lamport length  message
#> 1       0      5 greeting
#> 2       5      6 audience

# Show the document as it was after the first change
doc_checkout(doc, changes$frontiers[[1]])
text_get(text)
#> [1] "Hello"

# Return to the latest version
doc_checkout(doc)
text_get(text)
#> [1] "Hello world"
```

Subscriptions make live sync a one-liner, and undo reverses only local
edits.

``` r
a = loro_doc()
b = loro_doc()

# Send every update committed on `a` straight to `b`
sync = doc_subscribe_local_updates(a, function(bytes) doc_import(b, bytes))

# Track `a`'s local edits so they can be undone
manager = doc_undo_manager(a)

# Committing on `a` delivers the update to `b`
text_insert(a, 1, "Hello")
doc_commit(a)
text_get(b)
#> [1] "Hello"

# Undo is itself an edit, so it syncs to `b` too
undo(manager)
text_get(b)
#> [1] ""

# Stop syncing
unsubscribe(sync)
```

## Shiny example

An example app shows two replicas of one document side by side. Each
pane can be taken offline to make concurrent edits, which merge when it
comes back online. Below the panes a timeline shows every edit as a
bubble, in one row per replica above an axis of edit times; hovering a
bubble shows what was changed and by whom, and selecting one shows the
text at that point with the edit’s insertions and deletions highlighted.

``` r
shiny::runApp(system.file("examples/sync-editors", package = "creditor"))
```
